invitation.text: A short introduction shows you the most important things in about three minutes. You can also start it later with the ? button.

tour.intro: Optional, and you can stop at any time. You can also simply start on your own.
tour.restartAsk: Start again from the first step? Your stories stay as they are.
tour.finished: Well done: all steps are through. Every help topic is one click away.

board.title: Get to know the board
board.text: Every column is a status, every card is a story. Click the title of a card to open the story.

move.title: Move a story
move.text: Drag any story into another column. With the keyboard: choose the card, press Space, use the arrow keys, press Space again. The step is ticked off by itself.

create.title: Create a story
create.text: Press Ctrl+N or use the “New story” button. The step is ticked off when the story exists.

order.title: Order the backlog
order.text: Open the Backlog and drag a story to another place, or move it with the keyboard like on the board.

board.move.title: Move a story
board.move.keywords: status column drag drop keyboard arrow change
board.move.body:
Drag a card into another column to change its status. With the keyboard, choose the card, press Space to pick it up, move it with the arrow keys and press Space again to drop it. Escape cancels.
The change is saved at once.

board.columns.title: Columns and status values
board.columns.body:
Every column of the board is a status value. The columns belong to the categories To do, In progress and Done.
You can rename, add or remove status values under Settings, Status values.

story.open.title: Open and edit a story
story.open.keywords: story detail dialog title description criteria points click
story.open.body:
Click a story (anywhere on its card or row), or choose the card and press Enter, to open it. In the dialog you change title, description, points and status, and tick off the acceptance criteria.
Press Escape to close the dialog.

story.create.title: Create a story
story.create.body:
Press Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on a Mac) or use the “New story” button on the Board or the Backlog. Give the story a title and save it with the button or with Ctrl+Enter. If the title is missing, a message under the field says so.
“Add and add another” (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) keeps epic, sprint and points for the next story.
A new story starts in the first column.

story.menu.title: Change a story from its menu
story.menu.keywords: context menu right click status sprint epic points shift f10 move
story.menu.body:
Right-click a card or row (or choose it and press the menu key or Shift+F10). The menu changes status, sprint, epic and points without opening the story.
Use the arrow keys to move through the menu, the right arrow to open a submenu, Enter to choose and Escape to close.
A notice tells you what changed, and the story is framed in green for a moment.

story.quickAdd.title: Add stories quickly
story.quickAdd.keywords: quick add plus story column sprint cell title enter
story.quickAdd.body:
Click “+ Story” at the end of a column on the Board or of a section in the Backlog, or the “+” in a cell of the Story Map. Type a title and press Enter: the story is added in that place and the field stays open for the next one. Escape closes the field.
Only the title is asked; points, epic and the rest you can add later in the story.

backlog.order.title: Order the backlog
backlog.order.body:
The backlog is ordered by priority: the story at the top is the most important. Drag a row to another place, or move it with the keyboard: Space to pick up, arrow keys to move, Space to drop.
A story you drop into another sprint section is planned in that sprint.

backlog.sprints.title: Backlog and the sprint line
backlog.sprints.keywords: sprint planning section line upcoming running
backlog.sprints.body:
The backlog shows the sprints one below the other, followed by the stories that are not planned yet. The sprint line is the border between two sections: what is above it belongs to that sprint. Running and planned sprints are marked; completed sprints are no longer shown.
Drag stories across the line to plan them.

backlog.velocity.title: Velocity
backlog.velocity.keywords: velocity average planned completed points sprint chart table team capacity
backlog.velocity.body:
The Backlog shows the velocity of your team above the sprints: for each completed sprint two bars, the points planned when it was started and the points done. A dashed line shows the average of the last three completed sprints.
Hover over or tab to a sprint to see its dates, the share done and what joined during the sprint. “Older sprints” shows eight more; “Table” lists all sprints with the same values. Fold the panel with its title.
Every open sprint in the Backlog, on the Story Map and in the start dialog shows its points next to the average, for example “30 planned · Ø 21”. Use it to plan the next sprint realistically. The panel appears once you complete a sprint.

sprint.lifecycle.title: Start and complete a sprint
sprint.lifecycle.keywords: sprint start complete close finish end planned running ended unfinished stories next sprint
sprint.lifecycle.body:
A sprint is planned, running or completed. Only one sprint runs at a time; the board shows it.
To start a sprint, open the board while no sprint runs: it shows the next planned sprint. Press “Start sprint”, check its stories and points and confirm. These points count as planned.
To complete the running sprint, press “Complete sprint” on the board. The summary shows what was planned at the start, what is done and what joined or left during the sprint. Choose where the unfinished stories go: the next sprint, a new sprint or the backlog. Tick “Then start …” to start the next sprint right away.
A sprint whose end date has passed stays on the board, marked “ended”, until you complete it. A completed sprint disappears from the board, the backlog and the story map.

map.basics.title: Story Map
map.basics.keywords: map activities epics sprints rows columns release planning release board feature
map.basics.body:
The Story Map has one column per epic and one row per sprint. Every cell holds the stories of that epic in that sprint.
Drag a story into another cell to change its sprint and epic.
To plan by release instead of by sprint, first switch the feature “Releases” on (Settings → Features), then choose “Releases” as the rows (Settings → Story map).

epics.basics.title: Epics
epics.basics.body:
Epics group stories that belong together. Click an epic to rename it, change its colour or delete it.
An epic that still has stories cannot be deleted.

releases.basics.title: Releases
releases.basics.keywords: release version scope burndown history feature activate switch on enable toggle story map rows release board
releases.basics.body:
Releases only work when the feature “Releases” is switched on. Do it in this order:
1. Switch the feature on under Settings → Features. The page Releases then appears in the navigation.
2. Open the Releases page to create a release and to see its scope, progress and history.
3. To plan by release on the story map, choose “Releases” as the rows of the story map under Settings → Story map. The Story Map then shows one row per release.
If you switch the feature off again, everything about releases is hidden, but kept.

settings.basics.title: Settings
settings.basics.keywords: fields status values features story map rows gear switch on activate
settings.basics.body:
Open the settings with the gear button. They have four sections:
Fields describe your stories. Status values are the columns of the board. Story map sets the rows of the Story Map. Features switch parts of the app on or off, for example Releases.
The gear takes you back to the page you came from.

search.basics.title: Search
search.basics.keywords: find filter ctrl+f field status epic sprint
search.basics.body:
Press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) to search stories, epics and sprints. Several words must all occur; text in double quotes is searched as a phrase.
Narrow the search with filters such as status:done: type @ to see all fields.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body:
?  Open or close the help.
Ctrl+/  Show all keyboard shortcuts.
Ctrl+F  Search.
Ctrl+N  Create a story, an epic or a release, depending on the page.
Ctrl+Enter  Save a dialog for something new. Ctrl+Shift+Enter  Save a new story and add another.
Shift+F10 or the menu key  Open the menu of the chosen card.
Space, arrow keys, Space  Pick up, move and drop a card or row.
Escape  Cancel, or close a dialog or the help.
